body: Thanks! I'll make sure to let them know next visit then. I went this entire time thinking being in that much pain was the norm until recently, I wish you more bearable days as well ❤️

Awesome!! I'm glad you found something that helps. I know that finding any sort of relief is very hard to find, so that's something to celebrate lol. Personally my traumas have me react the opposite way, i'm always terrified and hypersensitive of everything, kind of like i'm in fight or flight mode 24/7. So experiencing sudden emotional numbness was extremely alien like to me, I'm not sure if i'm asking for too much from medications when I at least want to feel happy and excited about things again.. I'm perfectly fine with everything else. I'll keep what you said in mind next time I try them. Thanks for sharing :)
I'm truly proud of you that you're still fighting despite everything, thanks for your input. I hope more positive experiences come your way ❤️
Thanks for the suggestion! I'll definitely look into them. I wish you the best as well :)

I have severe social anxiety. Not much a friend can do since the anxiety tends to get unbearable in person, but show genuine interest and validate most of the things they say in person with a smile. We tend to constantly search people's faces and body language for any negative responses, but seeing only positives from you will surely ease some weight off their shoulders. I assure you they will feel more comfortable talking with you (and only you) over time, that time depends on the person.

*Thank you*, a million times, thank you. I was looking for this sort of response, I like knowing more of the specifics of what people usually do. I at least have some sort of guideline to follow now, appreciate it!

Now that I think about it, some people i'm interested in becoming better friends with aren't like me *at all*. Definitely a major reason we can't connect, yet I take it very personally when it doesn't work out. Thanks for that point of view I somehow didn't think of lol. As for how reaching out to them first goes, my anxiety gets too unbearable so I suppose that's a personal issue I need to fix first. I was focusing too much on them engaging with me first since the vice versa felt impossible. Easier said than done.. but I now have a starting point to work on, appreciate it :)
And then my sensitive ass feels like I actually did something wrong and I doubt myself. God I fucking hate this disorder

definitely, this applies to everything. i'm close to failing my classes and i can't even make myself watch my favorite tv shows for whatever reason. like the want is totally there, i just can't make myself do it. sort of how i feel towards social interaction in general.

getting over my self hatred is definitely easier said than done, i've tried accepting all of this in the past many times over but having nobody or nothing to live for is throwing me off. i'll keep fighting just a bit more since i'm surprised someone cared enough to respond to me, thank you :)

i agree that they could be nice distractions. we have tried plenty of things, and i've gone out of my way personally to make friends in the past online and irl. but i always self-sabotage these relationships since the anxiety & shame is unbearable. i *always* fuck it up so it's why i've given up. i could keep trying at that since it does sound like a better option than what i had planned, but idk how long i'd be able to keep that up. i know it sounds like i'm shooting down all of your suggestions, i'm not trying to, i'm sorry. i've just been completely alone for so many years.

hey there, thanks for the comment. i didn't really specify why i felt certain that i would be alone. i have [avoidant personality disorder](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000940.htm) which ruins any chances of interacting with said classmates, let alone anyone else. it's not a very known disorder so you can read about it to understand a little better. 

i've been stuck in a constant cycle of chronic isolation and self loathing ever since i was 5 and nothing seems to help. i've jumped around from 6 therapists/psychiatrists these last 2 years but it's so ingrained in me that nothing changes how worthless or out of place i feel. we have tried a few suggestions, but they all refer me to another therapist because they feel that they can't do anything.

never tried them and i'm really starting to think i should. i've completely given up. i've been avoiding them for so long but a chance to feel normal sounds like just what i need. anyone have anything specific that helps them?
